title: Evidence: checks not run when nothing in scope changed
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24 (imports end in .ts, erasable syntax only, no packages). Read the verify.evidence node in src/nodes/agent.ts (scope repair: `stray`, `if (stray.length && stray.length < changed.length)`, `const skip = p.mode === "edit" && diffLines === 0`, the evidence log line), `interface Evidence` in src/types.ts, and test/guards.ts + src/adapters/mock.ts (mock script: edits, stray, say, review).
Real-run problem: when EVERY change is outside ALLOWED FILES the stray files stay and the checks run on them, so the log says `scope VIOLATED, checks 1/1` and the pass looks like evidence. With no changes it says `checks 0/0`.
1. src/types.ts Evidence: add `/** Why the checks were not run (no changes, or only out-of-scope changes). */ checksSkipped?: string;`.
2. agent.ts verify: skip the checks for an edit agent when diffLines === 0 (reason "no changes") or when every changed file is out of scope (reason "every change is outside ALLOWED FILES"); store the reason as evidence.checksSkipped. The log line then reads `checks not run (<reason>)` instead of `checks x/y`. Keep everything else (checksOk stays checks.every(...); decisions are unchanged: scope VIOLATED still blocks accept).
3. Create test/verify.ts by copying the setup pattern of test/guards.ts (temp repo with a.js and check.js, mock models senior + coder, loadConfig override, Agents copied, engine.start): the mock coder has NO edits and one stray file notes.txt. Assert the task is not accepted, its last attempt has evidence.checks.length === 0 and evidence.checksSkipped matching /outside ALLOWED FILES/. Print `verify PASS`.
4. package.json: append ` && node test/verify.ts` to the test script.
Change nothing else.

title: Report: drop follow-ups that are another task's work
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read `followUps` and the report.final node in src/nodes/flow.ts (it builds `notes` from followUps(report) per task). Real run: agents listed other tasks' work as their follow-ups ("bin/test.js is owned by task t4", "t5 should document ...").
1. In flow.ts add `export function ownFollowUps(items: string[], otherIds: string[]): string[]` that drops items mentioning any other task id as a whole word (also inside backticks), e.g. id t4 matches "task t4", "`t4`", "t4's" but not "t40" or "st4". Escape ids for the regex.
2. In report.final use it for the agent notes only: `ownFollowUps(followUps(report), s.tasks.filter((x) => x.id !== t.id).map((x) => x.id))` (review findings, reverted and left-undone lines unchanged).
3. test/pick.ts (before `pick PASS`): assert ownFollowUps(["owned by task t4", "`t4` sets the script", "t40 is fine", "add a cache"], ["t4"]) deepEquals ["t40 is fine", "add a cache"]. Import it from ../src/nodes/flow.ts.
Change nothing else.

title: Senior question options become resume choices
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read the senior.understand node in src/nodes/senior.ts (it sets `s.waiting = { kind: "question", question, options: ["answer"] }`; on resume it appends `Owner answers: ${s.input.note || s.input.choice}` to s.request) and `arr`/`asText` at the end of the file (asText renders options as `Options: (1) a (2) b`). engine.resume only accepts a choice listed in waiting.options. Models often return questions as objects: {question, whyBlocking, options: string[]}.
1. Add `export function questionChoices(raw: unknown): string[]`: if raw is an array whose FIRST element is an object with a non-empty `options` array, return ["1", "2", ...] (one per option); else [].
2. In understand: options become `["answer", ...questionChoices(data.questions)]`. On resume, when the choice is one of those numbers, the answer text is that option's text, parsed back from s.waiting.question (the `(N) text` part, up to ` (N+1) ` or the end of that line), followed by ` (note: <note>)` when a note is given. For the choice "answer" keep today's behaviour.
3. test/guards.ts, next to the existing arr() assertions: questionChoices([{question: "q", options: ["a", "b"]}]) deepEquals ["1", "2"]; questionChoices(["plain"]) and questionChoices(undefined) deepEqual [].
Change nothing else (src/types.ts is not in your files).

title: orch summary: show working tasks and skipped checks
brief:
TypeScript run directly by Node 24. Read runSummary in src/ship.ts. Evidence (src/types.ts) now has `checksSkipped?: string`.
1. A task with status "running" and no attempt yet shows `working (attempt 1)` instead of "not started"; a running task whose last attempt has no decision yet shows `<model> working (attempt N)`.
2. In the checks text: when ev.checksSkipped is set, show `checks not run (<reason>)` instead of "no checks".
Change nothing else.

title: OpenHands: input tokens without cache reads; cache reads stored apart
brief:
TypeScript (Node 24, imports end in .ts) and one Python file. OpenHands runs report ~600k input tokens per task: scripts/openhands_agent.py (lines ~90-95) sets `input_tokens = u.prompt_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens = u.cache_read_tokens`; prompt_tokens already INCLUDES cache reads (LiteLLM convention), and src/adapters/cli.ts (parse "claude-json", ~line 111) adds input + cache_read + cache_creation, so cache reads are counted twice.
1. openhands_agent.py: input_tokens = max(0, prompt_tokens - cache_read_tokens).
2. src/types.ts: add optional `tokensCached?: number` to RunResult and to Attempt (next to tokensIn). src/vault.ts: add optional `tokensCached?: number` to Execution, and in the attempt note line that prints `tokens ${a.tokensIn}/${a.tokensOut}` append ` (+N cached)` when tokensCached > 0.
3. cli.ts claude-json: tokensIn = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens; tokensCached = cache_read_input_tokens; return tokensCached in the RunResult.
4. src/nodes/agent.ts: where attempts and executions record tokensIn (~lines 180 and 270), also record tokensCached (rounded) when present.
Change nothing else; other adapters may leave tokensCached undefined.
